lesson.menu_title: Three Questions in One — and the Formal Recommendation
lesson.menu_desc: Answering a multi-part question without losing the thread, and putting a recommendation on the table -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- Three Questions in One
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernando Meneghelli Bottura | Lesson 13 -- Three Questions in One

listenings.text: The three-part question is not an accident and it is not the interviewer being disorganised. It is a deliberate test, and what it tests is whether you can hold a structure in your head while you are also producing content. Most candidates answer the last part, because it is the one still in short-term memory, and then trail off. A few answer all three in a row and sound like a list. What we are actually listening for is the person who says, out loud, that there are three parts and which one they are taking first. That sentence costs four seconds and it changes everything, because from that moment the burden of remembering has moved from you to the room. And there is a second reason it works. If you name the three parts and then only answer two well, the interviewer will ask for the third rather than write down that you missed it. Naming the structure buys you a second chance you would not otherwise have had.

There are three parts to that, and I will take the middle one first because the other two depend on it. On governance, my recommendation would be that the audit committee review the reconciliation policy before the year end, not after it, on the grounds that the same exception has now appeared twice. On the systems question, it is not imperative that we decide this quarter, and I would caution against deciding before we have the migration cost. And on the third, which was whether I would keep the current controller structure, my answer is no, and I would put forward a single shared function instead. I should say that the second of those three is the one I am least certain about, and if the board wanted to defer it by a quarter I would not argue.

extra_audio.text: Beatrice asks a question with three separate parts inside it. Fernando says out loud that there are three parts and which one he will take first. Fernando gives a formal recommendation on governance with the reason attached. Fernando cautions against deciding the systems question this quarter. Beatrice asks which of the three he is least certain about.
